body.translated_text: Success! Homage to the noble <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet), the Blessed One!

body.text: evaṃ mayā śrutam ekasmin samaye bhagavān deveṣu trayastriṃśeṣu viharati sma pāṇḍukambalaśilāyām* / atha khalu śakro devānām indro 'surair jitaḥ parājitaḥ satvaraṃ tvaramāṇarūpo yena bhagavāṃs tenopasaṃkrāntaḥ / upasaṃkramya bhagavataḥ pādau śirasābhivandya bhagavantam etad avocat* / ihāhaṃ bhagavan vemacitriṇāsurendreṇa jitaḥ parājito devās trayastriṃśāś ca jitāḥ parājitāḥ / tatrāsmābhir bhagavan kathaṃ pratipattavyam* / bhagavān āha / udgṛhṇa tvaṃ devendra dhvajāgrakeyūrānāmadhāriṇīm aparājitāṃ yā mayā pūrvaṃ bodhisatvabhūtenāparājitadhvajasya tathāgatasyāntikād udgṛhītā / udgṛhya parebhyo vistareṇa saṃprakāśitā / nābhijānāmi tato 'rvāg bhayaṃ vā stambhitatvaṃ vā romaharṣanimittaṃ vāntaśaḥ kṣaṇikām api kāyapīḍām* /
body.translated_text: Thus have I heard. At one time, the Blessed One was dwelling among the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> (Thirty-three) gods upon the <s>Pāṇḍukambalaśilā</s> (Yellowish Woolen Stone). Then <s>Śakra</s>, lord of the gods, having been defeated and vanquished by the <s>Asuras</s>, hastily and with urgent manner approached the Blessed One. Having approached, he bowed his head at the feet of the Blessed One and said this to him: "Here, O Blessed One, I have been defeated and vanquished by the <s>Asura</s>-lord <s>Vemacitrin</s>, and the <s>Trāyastriṃśa</s> gods have been defeated and vanquished. How should we respond to that, O Blessed One?" The Blessed One said: "Take up, O lord of the gods, the <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) called <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet), the invincible, which I formerly, when I was a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, received from the <s>Tathāgata</s> <s>Aparājitadhvaja</s> (Unconquered Banner). Having received it, I proclaimed it extensively to others. I do not recall from that time onward any fear, or paralysis, or occasion for hair standing on end, or even a momentary bodily affliction."

body.text: tat katamā sā bhagavan dhvajāgrakeyūrā nāma dhāriṇī aparājitā /
body.translated_text: "What then, O Blessed One, is that invincible <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) called <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet)?"

body.text: tadyathā oṃ jaya 2 vijaya 2 jayavāhini śaṅkari bhayaṅkari prabhañjani rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca / pratyarthiko vā pratyamitro vābhidravati / oṃ jambhaya 2 stambhaya 2 mohaya 2 bhagavati jayavāhini matha matha pramatha pramatha grasa grasa hasa hasa hūṃ hūṃ lambha lambha lambodari trinetre caturvaktre caturdaṃṣṭre caturbhuje asimuśalacakratriśūlavajrakavacamudrādhāriṇi rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca bhagavati sarvopadravopasargopāyāsebhyaḥ / he he bhagavati hana hana daha daha paca paca matha matha pramatha pramatha dhuna dhuna vidhuna vidhuna hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ* bhañja bhañja parasainyaṃ vidhvaṃsaya āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajrasya saparivārasya sarvaśatrūn* / dhvajāgrakeyūre tṛṭa tṛṭa tṛṭu tṛṭu ulkādhāriṇi trailokyamathani vidhvaṃsaya parasainyam* / rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca sarvopadravebhyaḥ / cala cala cili cili culu culu kala kala kili kili kulu kulu muñca aṭṭaṭṭahāsam* / vidhvaṃsaya parasainyaṃ trāsaya 2 bhrāmaya 2 buddhasatyena dharmasatyena saṃghasatyena satyavādināṃ satyena / buddhasatyaṃ mātikrāma / dharmasatyaṃ mātikrāma / saṃghasatyaṃ mātikrāma / satyavādināṃ satyaṃ mātikrāma / lambodari 2 kuṭa kuṭa kuṭṭa kuṭṭa rudram ānaya / viṣṇum ānaya / candrasūryam ānaya / trailokyādhipatim ānaya / sarvadevatādhipatim ānaya / sarvadevatān ānaya / sarvayakṣarākṣasakumbhāṇḍamahoraganāgān ānaya / vidhvaṃsaya parasainyam* / raṅga raṅga raṅgāpaya raṅgāpaya jvala jvala puṣpamālini rundha rundha riṭi riṭi ciṭi ciṭi bhṛkuṭī mukhi parasainyaṃ kulomodanakari hala hala hili hili hulu hulu hūṃ hūṃ he he riṇi riṇi riṇamati jambha / dhvaje buddhāvalokite rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśriālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca sarvatathāgatāvalokite svāhā / guṇarājaprabhāse svāhā / sūryārkavimale svāhā / candrārkavimale svāhā / sarvagrahanakṣatradhyāmīkaraṇe svāhā / hūṃ hūṃ rakṣa rakṣa āvadhūtaśrīālakhavajraṃ saparivāraṃ sarvasatvāṃś ca sarvabhayebhyaḥ svāhā //
body.translated_text: It is as follows: <s>Oṃ</s>, be victorious, be victorious! Be supremely victorious, be supremely victorious! O bearer of victory, O auspicious one, O terrifying one, O destroyer! Protect, protect <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> together with his retinue and all beings! Whether an adversary or an enemy attacks — <s>Oṃ</s>, paralyze, paralyze! Petrify, petrify! Bewilder, bewilder! O Blessed One, bearer of victory, crush, crush! Thoroughly crush, thoroughly crush! Devour, devour! Laugh, laugh! <s>Hūṃ hūṃ</s>! Seize, seize! O pot-bellied one, O three-eyed one, O four-faced one, O four-fanged one, O four-armed one, O bearer of the sword, pestle, discus, trident, <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt), armor, and <s>mudrā</s> (seal)! Protect, protect <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> together with his retinue and all beings, O Blessed One, from all calamities, misfortunes, and troubles! He he, O Blessed One! Strike, strike! Burn, burn! Cook, cook! Crush, crush! Thoroughly crush, thoroughly crush! Shake, shake! Violently shake, violently shake! <s>Hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ</s>! Shatter, shatter the enemy army! Destroy all enemies of <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> and his retinue! O <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet)! <s>Tṛṭa tṛṭa tṛṭu tṛṭu</s>! O bearer of the firebrand, O crusher of the three worlds, destroy the enemy army! Protect, protect <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> together with his retinue and all beings from all calamities! <s>Cala cala cili cili culu culu kala kala kili kili kulu kulu</s>! Release a thunderous laugh! Destroy the enemy army! Terrify, terrify! Confound, confound! By the truth of the <s>Buddha</s>, by the truth of the <s>Dharma</s>, by the truth of the <s>Saṃgha</s>, by the truth of those who speak truth! Do not transgress the truth of the <s>Buddha</s>! Do not transgress the truth of the <s>Dharma</s>! Do not transgress the truth of the <s>Saṃgha</s>! Do not transgress the truth of those who speak truth! O pot-bellied one, O pot-bellied one! <s>Kuṭa kuṭa kuṭṭa kuṭṭa</s>! Bring <s>Rudra</s>! Bring <s>Viṣṇu</s>! Bring the Moon and Sun! Bring the lord of the three worlds! Bring the lord of all deities! Bring all deities! Bring all <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Rākṣasas</s>, <s>Kumbhāṇḍas</s>, <s>Mahoragas</s>, and <s>Nāgas</s>! Destroy the enemy army! Color, color! Cause to color, cause to color! Blaze, blaze! O garland of flowers! Obstruct, obstruct! <s>Riṭi riṭi ciṭi ciṭi</s>! O frowning-faced one, O maker of tumultuous joy against the enemy army! <s>Hala hala hili hili hulu hulu hūṃ hūṃ he he riṇi riṇi riṇamati jambha</s>! O banner beheld by the <s>Buddha</s>! Protect, protect <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> together with his retinue and all beings! O one beheld by all <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Guṇarājaprabhāsa</s> (Radiance of the King of Virtues), <s>svāhā</s>! To the immaculate sun, <s>svāhā</s>! To the immaculate moon, <s>svāhā</s>! To the darkener of all planets and <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar mansions), <s>svāhā</s>! <s>Hūṃ hūṃ</s>! Protect, protect <s>Āvadhūtaśrī Ālakhavajra</s> together with his retinue and all beings from all fears, <s>svāhā</s>!

body.text: iyaṃ sā devendra dhvajāgrakeyūrā nāma dhāriṇī aparājitā / yatra kvacid gacched yuddhe vā kalahe vā vigrahe vā vivāde vā sarvatra vijayo bhaviṣyati / dhvajāgre kaṇṭhe vā baddhvā dhārayitavyā manuṣyarājñā śūrapuruṣāṇāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ rakṣāṃ karoti / strīrūpadhāriṇī bhūtvā puratas tiṣṭhati / abhayaṃ dadāti rakṣāṃ karoti parasainyaṃ vidrāvayati / māṅgalyaṃ pavitraṃ śrīlakṣmīṃ saṃsthāpikā /
body.translated_text: This, O lord of the gods, is the invincible <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) called <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet). Wherever one goes, whether in battle, in conflict, in dispute, or in quarrel, there will be victory everywhere. It should be bound to the top of a banner or worn around the neck; it provides protection to human kings and to all heroic men. Taking the form of a woman, she stands before (the bearer). She grants fearlessness, provides protection, and puts the enemy army to flight. She is auspicious, purifying, and the establisher of <s>Śrī</s> (glory) and <s>Lakṣmī</s> (prosperity).

body.text: idam avocad bhagavān* / āttamanāḥ śakradevendras te ca bhikṣavas te ca bodhisatvā bhagavato bhāṣitam abhyanandann iti // //
body.translated_text: Thus spoke the Blessed One. <s>Śakra</s>, the lord of the gods, with joyful mind, along with those <s>bhikṣus</s> (monks) and those <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, rejoiced in the words spoken by the Blessed One.
The noble <s>dhāraṇī</s> (protective spell) called <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet) is completed.

body.text: oṃ bhagavati dhvajāgrakeyūre parasainyavidhvaṃsanakari / svasainyaparipālanakari / ulkāmukhi / kha kha / khāhi khāhi / parasainyam anantamukhenānantabhujena prahara prahara / hūṃ hūṃ / phaṭ phaṭ svāhā //
body.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, O Blessed <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet)! O destroyer of enemy armies! O protector of one's own army! O firebrand-faced one! <s>Kha kha</s>! Devour, devour the enemy army! Strike, strike with infinite faces and infinite arms! <s>Hūṃ hūṃ</s>! <s>Phaṭ phaṭ svāhā</s>!
The heart (essence) of the noble <s>Dhvajāgrakeyūrā</s> (Banner-Crest Armlet) is completed.
